topics.title: First to Tenth - Understanding Ordinal Numbers
topics.concept:
What are Ordinal Numbers?

Ordinal numbers tell us the position or order of something in a line or list. They answer the question "Which place?" not "How many?"

Cardinal Numbers vs. Ordinal Numbers:

Cardinal Number (How many?)Ordinal Number (Which position?)
1 (one)1st (first)
2 (two)2nd (second)
3 (three)3rd (third)
4 (four)4th (fourth)
5 (five)5th (fifth)
6 (six)6th (sixth)
7 (seven)7th (seventh)
8 (eight)8th (eighth)
9 (nine)9th (ninth)
10 (ten)10th (tenth)

How to Write Ordinal Numbers:

  • Most ordinal numbers add "th" to the end (fourth, sixth, seventh, tenth)
  • Special ones: first, second, third (they don't follow the rule!)
  • For numbers ending in 1, 2, 3 (except 11, 12, 13): use st, nd, rd

- 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th, ... 21st, 22nd, 23rd, 24th...

Remember the Special Ones:

  • 1 → first (not oneth!)
  • 2 → second (not twoth!)
  • 3 → third (not threeth!)
  • 5 → fifth (not fiveth - the 'v' changes to 'f')
  • 8 → eighth (only one 't')
  • 9 → ninth (drop the 'e')
  • 12 → twelfth (the 'v' changes to 'f')

examples.problem:
Who is in 3rd position in this line?

Line: Tom, Sam, Lily, Ann, Joe
examples.solution:
• 1st position = Tom
  • 2nd position = Sam
  • 3rd position = Lily

-

Answer: Lily **Example 2:** What is the ordinal number for the last runner if there are 8 runners in a race? *Solution:* - The last runner is in 8th place - 8th is written as "eighth" - **Answer:** 8th (eighth) **Example 3:** Draw 5 flowers in a row. Color the 2nd flower red and the 4th flower blue. *Solution:* - Draw flowers in positions: 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th - 2nd flower (second position) → color red - 4th flower (fourth position) → color blue - **Answer:** Flowers colored as instructed

recap: 4th to 10th add "th": fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth, tenth
Use ordinal numbers for: race positions, birthdays, floor numbers, dates
Ordinal numbers answer "Which one in order?"

topics.title: Position Concepts - Using Ordinal Numbers
topics.concept:
What are Position Concepts?

Position concepts help us describe where something is located using words like first, last, between, before, and after.

Key Position Words:

WordMeaningExample
**First**The one at the beginningThe first student in line
**Last**The one at the endThe last cookie in the jar
**Between**In the middle of two othersThe sandwich between the two books
**Before**Earlier in orderThe number before 5 is 4
**After**Later in orderThe number after 5 is 6

Finding Position in a Line:

  • Left to right: 1st is on the far left, last is on the far right
  • Right to left: 1st is on the far right, last is on the far left
  • Front to back: 1st is at the front, last is at the back

Using Ordinal Numbers in Sentences:

  • "I live on the 3rd floor."
  • "Today is my 5th birthday."
  • "December is the 12th month of the year."
  • "She came 2nd in the spelling bee."

examples.problem:
Look at this line: Apple, Banana, Cherry, Grape, Mango.

What fruit is in the 4th position?
examples.solution:
• 1st = Apple
  • 2nd = Banana
  • 3rd = Cherry
  • 4th = Grape

-

Answer: Grape **Example 2:** In a line of 10 children, Riya is 3rd from the front. What is her position from the back? *Solution:* - Total children = 10 - Position from front = 3rd - Position from back = 10 - 3 + 1 = 8th - Check: 1st, 2nd, 3rd (Riya), 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th - From back: 10th, 9th, 8th (Riya), 7th, 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd, 2nd, 1st ✓ - **Answer:** 8th **Example 3:** Tom is 4th in line. Sam is 3 places behind Tom. What position is Sam in? *Solution:* - Tom is 4th - 3 places behind means: 4 + 3 = 7 - Sam is 7th in line - **Answer:** 7th

recap: First = at the beginning, Last = at the end
Between means in the middle of two things
To find position from the back: (total + 1) - position from front
Ordinal numbers help describe order in daily life

topics.title: Everyday Applications of Ordinal Numbers
topics.concept:
Where Do We Use Ordinal Numbers Every Day?

Ordinal numbers are all around us! They help us understand order, sequence, and position in many real-life situations.

Common Everyday Uses:

SituationExampleOrdinal Used
**Birthdays**"Today is my 6th birthday!"6th (sixth)
**Race results**"She finished 1st in the race"1st (first)
**Dates**"December 25th is Christmas"25th (twenty-fifth)
**Floor numbers**"The library is on the 2nd floor"2nd (second)
**School grades**"I am in 1st grade"1st (first)
**Anniversaries**"It's our 10th wedding anniversary"10th (tenth)
**Sporting events**"He won 3rd place"3rd (third)
**Time order**"My first class is Math, second is Science"1st, 2nd

Ordinal Numbers for Dates:

DateWritten asOrdinal
June 1June 1stfirst
July 2July 2ndsecond
August 3August 3rdthird
September 4September 4thfourth
October 5October 5thfifth

Ordinal Numbers in Competitions:

  • 🥇 Gold medal = 1st place (First)
  • 🥈 Silver medal = 2nd place (Second)
  • 🥉 Bronze medal = 3rd place (Third)

examples.problem: Sarah's birthday is on March 12th. What ordinal number is this?
examples.solution:
• March 12th means the 12th day of March
  • "12th" is written as "twelfth"

-

Answer: twelfth (12th) **Example 2:** In a race, Tom finished 1st, Jerry finished 3rd, and Spike finished 5th. Who finished between Tom and Jerry? *Solution:* - 1st = Tom - 2nd = (someone) - 3rd = Jerry - The person between Tom and Jerry is in 2nd position - **Answer:** The person in 2nd place **Example 3:** A student has classes in this order: Math (1st), Science (2nd), English (3rd), History (4th), Art (5th). What subject is in the 4th period? *Solution:* - 1st = Math - 2nd = Science - 3rd = English - 4th = History - **Answer:** History

recap: Race results show order: 1st place, 2nd place, 3rd place
Dates use ordinal numbers: May 5th, June 1st, July 4th
Ordinal numbers help us understand sequence and order every day
